'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Mali War]]
**[[Mali wedding airstrike]]
***A report by the [[MINUSMA|United Nations mission in Mali]] concludes that an [[airstrike]] conducted by [[French Air and Space Force|France]] in [[Mopti Region|Mopti]] on January 3 killed 19 civilians at a wedding. The French military maintains that it had killed rebel fighters identified by aerial surveillance, and denies that a wedding had taken place in Bounti. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/3/30/french-air-attack-in-mali-killed-19-civilians-un-probe-finds (Al Jazeera)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)]]
**[[2021 Afghanistan attacks]]
***Gunmen kill three female [[polio]] [[vaccine|vaccination]] [[health worker]]s in [[Jalalabad]], [[Nangarhar]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/3/30/pakistan-afghanistan-hold-five-day-anti-polio-vaccination-drive (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2021–2022 Myanmar protests]]
**The death toll since the protests began officially surpasses 500. Pro-[[democracy]] activists launch a "garbage strike" in [[Yangon]] as rebel groups demand that the [[Tatmadaw|military]] stop the bloodshed or face retaliation. [https://www.dw.com/en/myanmar-protests-death-toll-passes-500/a-57046306 (DW)]
*[[Insurgency in Cabo Delgado]]
**Following the [[Battle of Palma|fall of Palma]] to [[Islamism|Islamist]] militants, [[Portugal]] announces it will be deploying 60 special forces troops to [[Mozambique]] in the coming weeks to train [[Mozambique Defence Armed Forces|local forces]] amid an intensifying insurgency. [https://www.france24.com/en/africa/20210330-portugal-to-send-troops-to-mozambique-after-brazen-palma-attack-by-islamic-insurgents (France 24)]
*A 65-year-old woman from the [[Philippines]] is critically wounded after being assaulted by a man during a [[racism|racist]] attack in [[New York City]]. The perpetrator, a man in his 30s who was previously in prison for murdering his mother, is charged with [[hate crime]] assault. [https://www.reuters.com/article/BigStory12/idUSKBN2BN167 (Reuters)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[President of the United States|President]] [[Joe Biden]] signs the PPP Extension Act of 2021, a bill that would extend the [[Paycheck Protection Program]] deadline from March 31 to May 31. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/ppp-extension-law-deadline-may-31/ (CBS News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in Italy]]
*****[[Prime Minister of Italy|Prime Minister]] [[Mario Draghi]] and his wife Maria Serenella Cappello receive their first doses of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://www.ansa.it/english/news/politics/2021/03/30/-draghi-vaccinated-with-astrazeneca-covid-19-jab-_ac46f780-d283-4bcf-9283-2b2ec3e8c976.html (ANSA)]
****The [[Government of Italy]] will impose a mandatory five-day [[quarantine]] for all travelers from other [[European Union]] member states until April 6. These travelers must also take a [[COVID-19 testing|COVID-19 test]] at the end of the quarantine period. The only exceptions are for reasons of "proven necessity and urgency". [https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20210330-italy-announces-five-day-covid-19-quarantine-for-eu-arrivals-over-easter (France 24)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****[[Germany|German]] health authorities suspend the use of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] vaccine in people under the age of 60 after new data showing a rise in unusual [[blood clot]]s in the head was released. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/german-state-suspends-astrazeneca-vaccine-60s-76766477 (ABC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Greece]] 
****[[Greece]] reports a record 4,340 new confirmed cases of [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 260,077. [https://www.ekathimerini.com/news/1158224/greece-breaks-new-record-in-new-virus-infections-intubations/ (''Ekathimerini'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]]
****[[Turkey]] reports a record 37,303 new confirmed cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 3.27 million. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/health/-over-37-000-new-covid-19-cases-reported-across-turkey/2193176 (Anadolu Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
****[[Brazil]] reports a record 3,780 [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|deaths]] from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thus bringing the nationwide death toll to 317,646. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/brazil-reports-highest-number-of-daily-covid-19-deaths/2193400 (Anadolu Agency)]
****[[Brazil]]'s health regulator [[Anvisa]] said [[Bharat Biotech]]'s [[Covaxin]] did not meet its manufacturing standards. The [[Government of Brazil|Brazilian government]] previously signed a contract to buy 20 million doses. Bharat said in a statement that they would appeal the decision. [https://riotimesonline.com/brazil-news/miscellaneous/covid-19/brazil-regulator-says-covaxin-immunizer-does-not-meet-factory-standards/ (''The Rio Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Venezuela]]
****[[Venezuela]] receives more than 115,000 doses of the EpiVacCorona [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] as part of trials of the Russian vaccine candidate. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-venezuela-russia/venezuela-receives-doses-of-russian-epivaccorona-vaccine-for-trials-idUSKBN2BM2VX (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ethiopia]]
***[[Ethiopia]] receives 300,000 doses of the [[Sinopharm]] [[BBIBP-CorV]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://www.thenationalherald.com/coronavirus/arthro/ethiopia_received_300k_doses_of_china_s_sinopharm_vaccine-2096332/ (''The National Herald'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Papua New Guinea]]
***[[Papua New Guinea]] begins a [[vaccination]] campaign against COVID-19 using the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] vaccine supplied from [[Australia]]. [[Prime Minister of Papua New Guinea|Prime Minister]] [[James Marape]] is the first person to receive a dose of the vaccine. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/mar/30/png-prime-minister-first-to-be-vaccinated-with-australian-supplied-doses-to-show-its-safe (''The Guardian'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan]]
***[[Pakistan]] reports 100 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, the highest recorded in a single day of the year so far, thus bringing the nationwide death toll to 14,434. The number of patients in critical care with COVID-19 also reaches an all-time high of 3,749. [https://www.dawn.com/news/1615587 (Dawn)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]], [[Lineage B.1.1.7]]
***Trials for the [[Novavax COVID-19 vaccine]] show that it is 90% effective against COVID-19 and the Lineage B.1.1.7 variant of [[SARS-CoV-2]]. [https://www.urdupoint.com/en/world/novavax-covid-19-vaccine-showing-really-exce-1208641.html (UrduPoint)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Sex trafficking in the United States]]
**An [[Matt_Gaetz_sexual_misconduct_allegations|investigation]] is opened into [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Rep.]] [[Matt Gaetz]] ([[Republican Party (United States)|R]]–[[Florida|FL]]) over whether he had a sexual relationship with a 17-year-old girl and violated federal sex trafficking laws by allegedly paying her to travel with him. Gaetz denied the allegations. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/03/30/us/politics/matt-gaetz-sex-trafficking-investigation.html (''The New York Times'')]
 
'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Hong Kong electoral reform]]
**China's [[Standing Committee of the National People's Congress|National People's Congress Standing Committee]] members vote in favor of amendments of the [[Hong Kong Basic Law]] Annex I and II to overhaul the [[Elections in Hong Kong|electoral system]]. The amendments are widely seen as a move to further reduce the influence of the opposition [[pro-democracy camp (Hong Kong)|pro-democracy camp]] in the wake of the [[2019–20 Hong Kong protests|widespread anti-government protests of 2019]] and the electoral landslide of the [[2019 Hong Kong local elections|2019 District Council election]]. [https://hongkongfp.com/2021/03/30/breaking-beijing-unanimously-approves-hong-kong-election-overhaul-reducing-democratic-representation/ (Hong Kong Free Press)]
*[[Presidency of Jair Bolsonaro]]
**In a meeting with recently-appointed [[Ministry of Defence (Brazil)|Defence Minister]] [[Walter Souza Braga Netto]] in the early hours of the day, the commanders of all three branches of the [[Brazilian Armed Forces]] – General [[Edson Leal Pujol]] ([[Brazilian Army|Army]]), Admiral [[Ilques Barbosa Junior]] ([[Brazilian Navy|Navy]]), and Brigadier [[Antonio Carlos Moretti Bermudez]] ([[Brazilian Air Force|Air Force]]) – announce their intention to resign from their posts as soon as new successors are found. The collective resignation announcement comes less than a day after the dismissal of former Defence Minister [[Fernando Azevedo e Silva]] and is allegedly a move to signal the Armed Forces' opposition to any military interference in politics. [https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/poder/2021/03/comandantes-militares-colocam-cargos-a-disposicao-e-descartam-golpismo.shtml (''O Estado de S. Paulo'')]

'''Sports'''
*[[2021 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament]]
**In college basketball, the [[2020–21 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|UCLA Bruins]] advance to the [[Final four|Final Four]] as an 11th seed after defeating the [[2020–21 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan Wolverines]], becoming the fifth team to do so after [[1985–86 LSU Tigers basketball team|LSU]] in [[1986 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|1986]], [[2005–06 George Mason Patriots men's basketball team|George Mason]] in [[2006 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|2006]], [[2010–11 VCU Rams men's basketball team|VCU]] in [[2011 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|2011]], and [[2017–18 Loyola Ramblers men's basketball team|Loyola–Chicago]] in 2018. They will also become the second team to reach the [[Final four|Final Four]] after starting in the First Four since the [[2010–11 VCU Rams men's basketball team|2011 VCU Rams]]. They will play the [[2020–21 Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball team|Gonzaga Bulldogs]], who defeated the [[2020–21 USC Trojans men's basketball team|USC Trojans]]. [https://www.si.com/college/cal/basketball/elite-eight-michigan-ucla (Sports Illustrated)]
